transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Martin Lowe (Head of Compliance, Aldercrest), Sofia Chen (CTO), Ravi Patel (DevOps), Elaine Murray (Legal)

Summary:
Aldercrest is evaluating hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC) for narrow set of financial workflows subject to GDPR and industry audit requirements. Primary concerns: encryption key residency, log retention and redaction, SSO/audit trails, and end-to-end evidence for model inferences. They want concrete artifacts (SOC2, ISO) and a runnable perf/latency test for decision. Timeline: internal decision in ~4 weeks, pilot to start mid-March if satisfied.

Topics covered:
- Deployment modes and tradeoffs (latency, cost, governance)
- Keystore residency and KMS/HSM options
- Log capture, redaction, and retention windows for regulated PII data
- Audit evidence for inferences and request-level tracing
- Canaries, fallbacks, and failover across regions
- Integration points: SAML SSO, RBAC, SIEM ingestion

Key questions asked:
- Can we keep keys in our AWS account or do you escrow?
- What level of request logs do you persist and for how long?
- How do you support GDPR right-to-be-forgotten for derivative model artifacts?
- Are there certifications and, if not, what evidence can you produce?

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, quick run through agenda—discuss hosting constraints, keystore, logs and evidence. Priya's going to jump into the technical bits.
[00:17] Martin Lowe: Hi, yeah thanks. We're juggling a few regulatory buckets, GDPR obviously, plus our auditors want a clear chain of custody for model decisions on loan adjudication. So, keystore residency is big for us.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Great, Martin. Just to be clear, when you say keystore residency do you mean customer-managed KMS in their VPC, or physical HSM on-prem?
[00:42] Martin Lowe: Ideally customer-managed KMS in AWS us-east with HSM-backed keys, but we need the option for keystore escrow if we go multi-region later.
[00:52] Sofia Chen: Also the logs—how do you handle raw prompt storage? We need to avoid storing PII verbatim, but also keep enough trace to reconstruct decisions during audits.
[01:05] Priya Shah: Right, so Redwood has a few levers — prefix/KV cache control, configurable request logging levels, and a redaction pipeline. For Private/Dedicated customers we can route logs to your SIEM and optionally disable full prompt capture—store hashes and metadata instead.
[01:23] Ravi Patel: When you say "disable full prompt capture" — does that still let us repro model outputs for drift investigations? We need replayability for specific cases.
[01:34] Priya Shah: Good question. There's a trade — if you redact PII tokens we can store a token-map in your VPC only so you can repro internally, but Redwood won't hold the mapping. That means replay is possible but we don't have access to the cleartext.
[01:50] Martin Lowe: That sounds promising. What about retention windows—our policy is 30 days for raw PII, 3 years for audit artifacts. Can Redwood conform?
[02:01] Jordan Ellis: We can support configurable retention per-tenant. Hosted customers get default 90 days for debug logs, but Dedicated/Private allow policy enforcement to your 30-day window for raw inputs and longer for hashed audit logs. We'll need to record that in the SLR / contract.
[02:18] Elaine Murray: On legal, we need to ensure we can put a data deletion clause that covers model derivative concerns — basically, if we ask you to purge, how do you certify that inferences and intermediate caches are removed?
[02:31] Priya Shah: There are a couple of pieces: KV cache eviction + full model warm start and cache wipe, index / embeddings deletion, and audit log truncation. For Dedicated we can run an e2e purge sequence and provide a signed attestation. For Hosted it's more complicated but we do provide evidence logs and deletion confirmations.
[02:50] Sofia Chen: Any gotchas around model variants? For example, if we use a quantized variant for cost, does that affect ability to do forensics or reproduce outputs?
[02:59] Priya Shah: Slightly — quantization can cause small numeric diffs that make bit-exact replay impossible across variants. We recommend pinning model versions for critical paths and using the same variant for audit-critical requests.
[03:12] Martin Lowe: Certifications—do you have SOC 2 or ISO? Auditors will ask for something concrete.
[03:17] Jordan Ellis: We have SOC2 Type II in progress and ISO scope underway. I will share our current security pack plus a redwood-specific architecture diagram.
[03:24] Martin Lowe: We've seen people say "Sock two" on calls and I just wanted to note we need the full report not just a high-level.
[03:31] Jordan Ellis: Understood, we'll include the report extract and point to the controls mapping.
[03:36] Ravi Patel: Network segmentation—if we go Private, how do you handle control plane access? Is there still a Redwood-managed control plane that can reach into our VPC?
[03:47] Priya Shah: For Redwood Private we can deploy with a customer-controlled control plane endpoint. The default is split plane: customer-facing data plane sits in your VPC and control plane runs in our environment but over mutually authenticated TLS with VPC peering or private link. For the strictest setups we can offer an air-gapped on-prem package.
[04:06] Sofia Chen: Does the control plane still need key-material access? We need to know if any key wrapping or ephemeral keys cross the network.
[04:14] Priya Shah: Best practice is to keep key material in your KMS/HSM and only provide wrapped keys. Redwood doesn't require raw key material. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs via PKCS#11.
[04:28] Elaine Murray: On data subject requests—if a EU citizen asks to be forgotten, models may have absorbed signals during training. How do you support that?
[04:38] Jordan Ellis: We clarify that Redwood serves inference only; we do not retrain customer models. For derivative concerns, we have processes to delete customer-provided prompt data and embeddings. For broader training corpora that's a separate discussion with model vendors.
[04:52] Martin Lowe: Okay. Another operational question—latency targets. For our loan decision flow we need p95 < 300ms. Can Redwood meet that on Hosted, or do we need Dedicated?
[05:03] Priya Shah: It depends on model size and sequence length. For small-ish models and short sequences hosted can hit that p95 in a nearby region; for consistent <300ms at scale, Dedicated with pinned capacity is more predictable. We can run an A/B bench — we'll test both hosted and dedicated to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:23] Ravi Patel: Cost is obviously a factor. We can't commit to a heavy reserved contract unless the numbers justify it. Are there burst policies if we go Dedicated?
[05:33] Jordan Ellis: Yes, Dedicated has configurable burst pools and autoscale policies. We'll include example SLOs and cost modeling in the deck.
[05:40] Sofia Chen: Regarding logging export—can you push logs to our Splunk? We want to centralize auditor views.
[05:47] Priya Shah: Absolutely. We support pushing structured logs to your SIEM via Kinesis, Pub/Sub, or syslog over TLS. For PII we recommend redaction at source and delivering a sanitized feed.
[05:58] Martin Lowe: Ok — about evidence for an audit: request->response mapping, timestamping, who called it (SSO identity). Do you emit those fields?
[06:07] Priya Shah: Yes, we emit request id, caller identity (if SSO provided), tenant id, model/version, region, and timestamp. We can optionally include trace-level token counts and latency breakdowns.
[06:18] Elaine Murray: Can we get deletion attestations signed by an authorized Redwood person? Our legal will want that.
[06:24] Jordan Ellis: Yes for Dedicated/Private we can do signed attestations post-purge. For hosted it's case-by-case but we provide deletion logs.
[06:33] Sofia Chen: Are there known limitations with geofencing? We have EU-only data flows for some classes.
[06:39] Priya Shah: We support region pinning and restricted routing so requests for EU-tagged tenants stay within EU regions. For stricter geofence we recommend Private deployment in your EU VPC.
[06:49] Martin Lowe: One more: does Redwood retain embeddings? We might want to store embeddings in our cluster only.
[06:55] Priya Shah: You can configure embeddings to be stored in your storage (S3 in your account) or Redwood-managed store. We recommend customer-managed for sensitive PII uses.
[07:05] Ravi Patel: Good. A quick thing—are there SDK hooks to obfuscate before send? We prefer client-side tokenization and hashing.
[07:12] Priya Shah: Yes, the SDK supports client-side hooks and pre-send processors. We also have examples for token scrubbing and on-device hashing.
[07:20] Jordan Ellis: I want to make sure we capture the decision criteria — Martin, can you speak to the top three success metrics?
[07:25] Martin Lowe: Sure: 1) Evidence and attestation to auditors (auditability), 2) Latency SLOs met consistently, and 3) Control of key material and logs. If those are green we can move to pilot.
[07:38] Jordan Ellis: Great. Timeline—you're aiming to decide in about four weeks?
[07:41] Sofia Chen: Correct, we have an internal steering committee on 2027-02-28. Pilot would start mid-March.
[07:48] Jordan Ellis: Ok action list — I'll send certs and security pack, Priya will share perf tests, and we'll schedule a follow-up demo for Dedicated.
[07:56] Elaine Murray: Also please include a sample contractual clause for deletion attestation.
[08:01] Jordan Ellis: Will do.
[08:05] Sofia Chen: Quick clarification — what do you call "Redwood Private"? On some docs we've seen "Redwood Privy" typoed, just making sure it's the private VPC option.
[08:13] Priya Shah: Yeah, that's a common transcription error—it's Redwood Private, VPC/on-prem option.
[08:18] Martin Lowe: One last nit—how do you handle cross-border operator access for support? We need a view of who can access logs in emergencies.
[08:30] Priya Shah: Access is role-based, logged, and requires approved JIT access for support sessions. We capture a support session recording and can confine access by IP and time windows.
[08:42] Ravi Patel: That helps.
[08:45] Jordan Ellis: Ok folks, we're at about 45 minutes — anything else?
[08:49] Martin Lowe: No that's it. We'll review the pack and get back about the pilot scope.
[08:54] Jordan Ellis: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.

Call end.

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional speaker labels include "Speaker 1" from recorder; some technical terms transcribed as "K V cash" or "Sock two". Natural pauses and crosstalk present.
